item.title: Pep-Talk Sticky Notes: Re: Pep-Talk Sticky Notes
item.content:encoded:
+ Cope Crit
- Close

Okay, here we go… Let's go over this, shall we?

A sticky note pad that is only useable by personnel currently experiencing negative emotions. When said personnel take one, the message on the note viewable only to them calms them down and leaves them feeling content for a period of three minutes afterward. When the three minutes are up, the subject is left in a neutral state. The messages are reported as upbeat and encouraging.

Why does the sticky pad do this? So far (in my eyes), it seems like a dumbed-down version of SCP-999. Other then encouraging people, is there anything else?

It logs how the anomaly is used during testing and ends with a log in which the notepad manifests a secondary anomalous property. It also logs the potential uses of the notepad.

This is not a Central Narrative. This would be put into Page Layout.

I plan the Containment Procedures to be attention-grabbing, with them going something like As SCP-XXXX poses no threat to the security and safety of Site-XX and its personnel, SCP-XXXX is allowed to be freely used whenever it manifests contained in a lock-protected drawer in Dr. XXXXX's office. Also, I plan to put an interview log in which the notepad manifests in the middle of a stressful interview and then manifests to the interviewee after failing the interview miserably.

This would also be in Page Layout. Also, could you expand on what you mean by "manifests"? Can it turn into something else. Also, Also, an interview? For who? Why? How would it correlate to your current idea. Can the sticky pad talk?

I know it's another item SCP, but they work best for my writing style. Also, I want to write this one to be easy to understand for people who have never read an SCP before.

Nothing is wrong with another item SCP. We have plenty of them and continue to have plenty of them. The key is making them new and unique with a different direction. So far, you haven't gone indepth with the SCP. I suggest you think more about the SCP. Read a few guides. They always help me. You can also seek help from the butterfly squad. They're always ready to help and much more experienced then myself.

http://www.scpwiki.com/guide-hub
http://www.scpwiki.com/butterfly-squad-roster

If you want to bounce ideas with me, I'd be more than happen to help you. You can PM me anytime.

- Close

item.title: Hive-Mind Wolves: Hive-Mind Wolves
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Page Layout (Optional): Large Special Containment Procedures and Description, as well as a brief addendum, and a video transcript.

Elevator Pitch: A group of three wolves that can see through opaque objects, but cannot see through transparent/translucent objects at all, any person seen by an instance can be elevated into a hostile, collective hive mind, however it has a limited range.

Central Narrative: These wolves can turn entire groups of people into collective hive minds, that are violent, and can cause mass destruction, people can be initiated into the hive mind almost instantly, but it takes 15 minutes out of sight of the instances to exit, requiring some pretty specific methods and tactics to prevent the hive mind from simply walking back into the SCP's line of sight, or allowing the SCP to breach containment entirely.

However, the SCP instances and the members of the hive minds appear to want to destroy the foundation, as those affected have been seen to destroy foundation buildings and locations before they would be held off.

It would be found somewhere in washington after attracting the attention of the foundation as a horde of people started raiding a foundation building, and started to essentialy dismantle and destroy it, before those people would be either kept away by task forces or neutralized to keep away if necessary. Several groups would have to get together to contain the SCP and lock it away in Area-14, in Nevada.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Just the pure speculation of the damage this SCP could do, due to it's ability to turn large masses of people into essentially their own weapon, while maintaining their individual intelligence such as ability to use weaponry and vehicles, as well as that the SCP and the hive minds appear to have a hatred or distaste for The Foundation, and seek to destroy or dismantle it.

Additional Notes: Nothing else much to say here, except, thank you for looking over this, and giving me your critique, and I'll do my best to pay attention.

item.title: The Lightswitch: Re: The Lightswitch
item.content:encoded:
The GOI then used this to its own advantage, killing targets and employees with high levels of skill/competence/important memories and then adding them to some central source (becoming a sort of librarian/bookkeeper of minds).

Honestly not sure why you need to go here… its much more interesting of an anomaly without the edgy "they used it to assassinate people" trope.

So the anomaly is interesting, but I feel your execution is fairly tropey. I'd be much more interested in a narrative about identity than about some mystical bad guy from a GOI.

Moreover, there's very little narrative here. As described it is a short concept that is focused on how the anomaly works, without more substantive storytelling.

I think this is a pretty novel idea, and could be used to tell an interesting story, so I would suggest workshopping some concepts that this anomaly could be used to explore.

item.title: Radio Virus SCP seeking green light: Re: Radio Virus SCP seeking green light
item.content:encoded:
Thank you very much for your critique. It really means a lot. The Announcer is responsible for the horde, but not aware of the hordes existence or his part in making it. This story is about what happens when a version of him finally learns about the true nature of himself and his “siblings”. As for the connection between the man and beast, it’s symbolic of having a dream fulfilled that a person thought they wanted, but the reality was a lot different than what they’d expected. As for in-universe explanation, the creatures are the enforcers, making sure that the Virus spreads by blocking out every other sound.

I hope that at least answers some of your questions. Have a happy holiday season.

item.title: J SCP: The Element of Surprise: J SCP: The Element of Surprise
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: J SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Joke SCP, Comedy

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP page

Elevator Pitch: An incident involving a Scranton Reality Anchor releases a new element into the atmosphere: the Element of Surprise. This element affects the Hume levels on a small area around it, creating unforeseeable results akin to Alchemy (transformation of one element into another, creating life, etc).

Central Narrative: Following the incident researchers notice that their experiments are yielding crazy results. Both super advanced experiments and simple stuff like making grilled cheese present impossible outcomes. The page shows reports of some failed experiments and the comically truncated investigation to understand the phenomenon. Finally they isolate the new element and devise a way to contain it: a multilayered sphere made of random materials that can resist the alterations caused by the Element of Surprise, maintenance includes adding new layers at random intervals to prevent ruptures.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:

  • Cartoon-like humor with the failed experiments
  • New element that can be used in future articles and tales

Additional Notes: I don't have a lot of expertise on Joke SCPs but this idea seemed worth investing on. I'm open to all crits and suggestions :)

item.title: IMAGINE YOU WERE THERE: Potential SCP: Re: IMAGINE YOU WERE THERE: Potential SCP
item.content:encoded:
+ Cope Crit
- Close

Okay, let's see what we have…. Beware. I'm blunt and straight to the point.

A sadistic man tells stories of violence and death. People who listen are entranced. However, as the story goes on, listeners start to show signs of physical trauma. When the man finishes his story, any wounds inflicted on the characters in the story appear on the listener, often killing them.

Okay, so he's a sadistic human that uses mind affecting abilities. I got that. But why? Why does he kill people? Why does he do what he does?

The concept is introduced in the Containment Procedures and Description. The SCP is relatively easy to contain, except that his anomalous abilities increase over time unless he is given a D-class to tell a story to. If he is not sated within 8 days, his anomalous abilities begin to work over video, radio, and recordings. If he cannot tell anyone a story in 15 days, he will begin to project mental images of torture and killing into the minds of people outside his containment. After 21 days, this starts to cause minor but real physical damage to those affected. After 28 days, he mentally projects his image of agony onto everyone within several kilometers, which kills most of those affected.

Okay, so you've talked about how his ability increases every day and it eventually kills people within several kilometers. How long does this last? Does it reset? Does it stay in a several kilometer range until it's finished? Either way, why don't they just lock him up in an cell outside that radius and just use other means to research the subject?

The SCP was discovered and contained after a series of anomalous murders in Tokyo. The SCP seems to understand more about its powers than the Foundation does, and has caused a number of incidents and containment breaches.

It sounds like he's just here to be a headache for the Foundation and nothing more, which brings me to my next thing.

In an interview, the SCP recounts its childhood psychopathy, its path to becoming a serial killer, and how it attained its anomalous abilities.

Care to expand on that? Up to this point you've only explained how much of a danger this guy is and his abilities. You haven't really talked about the narrative in any great detail.

Overall thoughts: Other then the fact that anomalous human affecting people's mind has been done before, this doesn't seem to have any unique concept. Just dangerous to be dangerous. You hinted at a story, but to no detail. Some of the points didn't seem to be needed either, like;

The concept is introduced in the Containment Procedures and Description.

What concept? The narrative? The abilities? I'm not sure what you're referring to.

If you could clear some stuff up, I could look over it again.

- Close

item.title: June the 31st: Re: June the 31st
item.content:encoded:
And…that didn't answer any questions, so putting it more bluntly:

1) This is a Keter-level event as it has the potential to see a lot of dead people, or at least inconvenienced ones. If fishermen are tracking a school of fish, this would put them a day behind, possibly causing them to miss a needed harvest. Unless doctors' idea of a great time is remaining on shift, you are going to see a lot of deaths as simple injuries become much more complicated due to the lack of immediate care; this even would encourage more bravery in individuals so you would see more accidents.

You would also see a lot of pregnancies result in deaths, as well as more mysterious pregnancies.

And if people are truly occupying their lives, expressing themselves fully, keep in mind that this frees all of those with murderous and other ill intents. If my idea of a tranquil day is one where I kill all of my enemies and rape their relatives, then just made that so much easier. And with all of the unprotected sex, you're going to see a huge spike in STDs.

In short, for most people it's going to be a day of picnics and rainbows, but for others it's going to be a day of blood and murder. There will be a lot of bodies.

2) The Foundation isn't going to be able to hide as many changes as you think. Not all clocks are hooked to the net, and you're ignoring a lot of obvious tells, such as weather patterns and animal movements.

3) You may be ignoring all of those other groups, but with The Foundation dealing with all of those bodies and other issues, this is going to leave them open to attacks on their sites. As such, you need to allow for that.

Straight up: This is an awesome horror event. Not so much a day of peace….

item.title: EVER EVASIVE BUBBLE!!! IN NEED OF GREENLIGHT!!!: EVER EVASIVE BUBBLE!!! IN NEED OF GREENLIGHT!!!
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: scp article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Elevator Pitch: This scp is a bubble with a folded note inside of it. the outside of the note is a face that looks like it is sleeping. the scp seeming to subconsciously avoid all forms of touching. Inside of the folded note may be a memetic symbol, a ground breaking discovery, or a piece of information so horrible, it could shatter even the most sturdy minds.

Central Narrative: This scp was found in a circus that came to [REDACTED] Wisconsin one in a while. A researcher was taking his kids to that circus one day and there was a sign that read ,"EVER-ELUSIVE BUBBLE!!! COME TRY TO POP IT!" the researcher, thinking it would be a great first circus game for them to try, took them into the tent. The kids jumped at the bubble, trying to pop it, and each time, the bubble unnaturally evaded the attempt. The research had called his site director and told him about it. Later after the circus closed, an MTF squad circled the perimeter and closed the circus down. The reason they told the local police and the circus members was because of "safety" and "Drug use". The circus is now a private site of the foundation. several cameras and MTF members have been placed around the perimeter. A monitor room has been placed just outside of the site to keep track of the property.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The note inside of the bubble could have anything in it.

item.title: Small SCP idea: JS Staff Post -- Forum Crit -- Info
item.content:encoded:
Author,

Per the required reading forum guidelines, please fill out the concept template to seek feedback on your idea:

 **Seeking Greenlights:** Put yes or no. **Page Type:** SCP Article, Tale, GoI Format, Joke SCP, Site Dossier, Other (specify) **Genre (Optional):** Horror, Drama/Emotional, Comedy, Action, History, Other (specify) **Page Layout (Optional):** [How will you will structure the page in terms of information presentation, or plot development? If you plan on using a unique format/format screw, describe that here.] **Elevator Pitch:** [What is the basic core idea? Use a bullet point list if necessary.] **Central Narrative:** [Describe the story beats or overarching context/"big picture" for your piece. If there is no story content, put "none".] **Hook/Attention-Grabber:** [What is novel/unique about your premise? What is special about your idea here that will make it stand out among the other works already on the mainsite?] **Additional Notes:** [Note any concerns or particular areas of assistance you would like reviewers to focus on.]

Rather than posting a new comment, edit your previous post using the "edit" function under the "options" tab to the lower right of your first comment.

Remember that the combined text for your answers to the last four sections (Elevator Pitch, Central Narrative, Hook/Attention-Grabber, and Additional Notes) MAY NOT exceed 400 words. For convenience, authors can use this page to check wordcount: https://wordcounter.net/

Once you have revised your post accordingly, please reach out to reviewers to request that they look at your thread. You can find example lists of contacts in the Required Reading thread linked above.
